questions.prompt: Why does log₂(x - 5) = log₂(1 - x) have no solution?
questions.prompt_markup: Why does log₂(x - 5) = log₂(1 - x) have no solution?

choices.text: Both sides are defined only if x > 5 and x < 1 at the same time, which is impossible.
Setting x - 5 = 1 - x gives x = 3, which is a solution, so the equation does have one.
The equation has a solution only when x is negative.
Logarithms with base 2 can never be equal to each other.

questions.correct_answer: Both sides are defined only if x > 5 and x < 1 at the same time, which is impossible.
questions.grading_note: The candidate x = 3 makes both arguments negative. The others accept x = 3 without checking the domain, invent a condition about negative x, or claim logarithms cannot be equal.

questions.prompt: How do the graphs of y = log₂ x + log₂(x - 2) and y = 3 show that the only solution is x = 4?
questions.prompt_markup: How do the graphs of y = log₂ x + log₂(x - 2) and y = 3 show that the only solution is x = 4?

choices.text: They intersect only at x = 4; the left graph exists only for x > 2, so there is no point at x = -2.
They intersect at x = 4 and at x = -2, so both values are solutions of the equation.
They never intersect, so x = 4 must come from the algebra only.
They intersect at y = 4, which is the solution of the equation.

questions.correct_answer: They intersect only at x = 4; the left graph exists only for x > 2, so there is no point at x = -2.
questions.grading_note: Graphs show only points in the domain.

questions.prompt: Why can ln x = 2 - x not be solved exactly with logarithm rules?
questions.prompt_markup: Why can ln x = 2 - x not be solved exactly with logarithm rules?

choices.text: ln x is undefined for every x, so the equation has no solution at all.
Logarithm rules apply only to equations with base-10 logarithms.
The equation has infinitely many solutions, so no single exact value exists.
x appears both inside a logarithm and outside it, so no algebraic step isolates x.

questions.correct_answer: x appears both inside a logarithm and outside it, so no algebraic step isolates x.
questions.grading_note: Such equations are solved with graphs or tables. The others are false: ln x is defined for x > 0, the equation has one solution, and the rules apply to every base.
